## 固定收益市場主線

10月14日，科技股跌勢加深，資金重新買進債券，長天期美債收復通膨消息引發的跌幅；短端則仍受聯準會可能再度升息的預期壓抑。10年期殖利率收在5.1854%，下降2.3個基點，2年期小升0.85個基點至4.7975%。殖利率曲線趨平，美國高收益債信用利差明顯擴大。

9月消費者物價是當日最關鍵的政策消息。汽油帶動整體通膨加速，基礎通膨又高於預期，使延至12月再升息的理由更難成立。聯準會地區企業調查也顯示，成本壓力正沿供應鏈傳遞；芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee則警告，AI投資可能使需求過熱。然而，當日最終呈現的是長期實質殖利率下降，而非整條美債曲線殖利率持續上升。CoreWeave債券跌至困境價位、半導體股大幅下挫，使AI建設的成本與能否持續，在通膨衝擊之外成為迫切的信用問題。

## 通膨壓力擴散，長天期美債仍收復跌幅

9月CPI公布後，市場最初反應強烈。據Bloomberg盤中報導，2年期殖利率一度上升16個基點至4.95%，5年期短暫突破5.15%，為2007年以來首見。投資人迅速提高對進一步緊縮的預期：期貨隱含的10月升息機率，由公布前約20%升至最高55%，其後回到約40%。市場一度完全反映截至1月底升息兩次、每次25個基點，稍後則反映同期約40個基點的升息幅度。

收盤前的反彈集中在最短天期以外的美債。5年期殖利率下降1.44個基點至4.9869%，30年期下降3.38個基點至5.5231%；2年與10年期利差收窄3.15個基點至38.79個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄4.23個基點至72.56個基點。股市跌勢加劇後，較高殖利率吸引債券買盤，逆轉早盤大部分跌幅。最終，對政策較敏感的2年期殖利率小升，中長天期債券價格則上漲。

抗通膨債券市場仍保留了CPI較令人不安的一面。10年期實質殖利率下降3.67個基點至2.8248%，但同天期損益兩平通膨率上升1.37個基點至2.3606%，實質殖利率的降幅超過通膨補償的增幅。一週來，10年期名目殖利率下降9.83個基點，30年期下降14.72個基點；以一個月比較，兩者仍分別上升21.74與16.91個基點。10年期的月度升幅仍主要來自實質殖利率：實質殖利率上升22.88個基點，損益兩平通膨率反而下降1.14個基點。

9月整體CPI月增0.6%，高於8月的0.4%，符合市場月增預估；年增率則由3.4%升至3.7%，超過預期的3.6%。排除食品與能源的核心CPI月增0.3%，與前月相同，但高於預期的0.2%；年增率由2.4%升至2.6%，也高於市場預估的2.5%。這是核心通膨連續第二個月高於預期，也是10月27日至28日政策會議前最後一次CPI公布。

汽油價格月增9.1%，但漲價不限於燃料。醫療照護服務與屋主設算租金各上漲0.3%；中古車價格上漲0.7%，為2025年10月以來最大月增幅。機票也漲價，食品雜貨價格則略降。電腦軟體與配件比一年前貴28.4%，創下紀錄；電腦、周邊設備及智慧家庭助理價格也以9.7%的年增幅創新高。這些科技品項顯示，運算容量的龐大投資需求之外，家庭購買科技產品所面對的價格壓力也已可量化。

Goolsbee週三在數據公布後表示，數字令人失望，服務通膨顯示壓力不只存在於受關稅與伊朗戰爭影響的品項。他更擔心資料中心建設與AI投資使經濟過熱，認為目前仍無法確定利率是否已高到足以讓通膨回到2%。他的重點是需求壓力的持續性：一旦過熱累積，要消除便更困難。

週三公布的褐皮書，以截至10月5日蒐集的資訊，補充了各地區的情況。聯準會12個轄區中，有一半回報物價壓力強勁或正在加劇。企業除能源之外，也提到其他原物料、關稅與保險成本，柴油附加費正將較高成本沿供應鏈傳遞。多數地區經濟仍有一定成長，整體就業變化不大或沒有變化；11個轄區至少出現部分薪資上漲，數個地區指出通膨正增添加薪壓力。

調查也說明，招聘疲弱未必等於生產疲弱。費城受訪製造商有逾三分之二表示第三季產量增加，占比為2022年第二季以來最高，成長範圍不限於資料中心、AI與國防。達拉斯回報耐久財與非耐久財製造業的產量、需求均增強，包括石油相關支出，以及維持高檔的煉油與石化活動。堪薩斯城製造商因難以找到或留住員工，增加工時與加班；克里夫蘭兩家銀行受訪者則表示，AI與自動化提高生產力，減少了人力需求。

家庭與小型企業承受的是另一面的成本壓力。紐約受訪者在續保健康保險時，面對保費大漲、自付額提高及較高的部分負擔。聖路易的雇主將部分保險成本轉嫁員工，一些非營利組織則縮減或取消雇主負擔的福利。亞特蘭大高價位零售需求增強，其他價格帶需求卻持平或下降；舊金山受訪者表示，財務壓力正由低收入家庭擴散到中等收入家庭。週三另一項數據顯示，經通膨調整的每小時薪資已連續第六個月較去年同期下降。

房市提供了貨幣緊縮的最新跡象。MBA的30年期房貸利率在截至10月9日當週上升1個基點至7.50%，為2023年11月以來最高，並比6月底高出近1個百分點。購屋貸款申請減少4%，連續第六週下降，為2023年7月至8月以來最長連跌；購屋申請指數由145.1降至139.3。轉貸申請連續第八週下滑，指數由515.8降至513.5。整體房貸申請繼前週減少4.2%後再降2.7%，總指數由204.7降至199.2。全美房地產經紀人協會首席經濟學家Lawrence Yun預期，較高利率將減少第四季完成交割的交易；先前的成交仍反映最近這波融資壓力升高前簽訂的契約。

通膨壓力擴散也使花旗修改政策預測。經濟學家Veronica Clark與Andrew Hollenhorst原先預期利率維持不變至2027年第一季，如今改估12月升息25個基點，但仍預期之後降息。PGIM的Robert Sockin表示，數據強化了他原有的10月升息預測。Principal Asset Management的Seema Shah，以及道明證券的Oscar Munoz與Gennadiy Goldberg，仍預期12月升息；道明認為，市場利率上升已提供部分抑制效果。Janney的Guy LeBas則認為，需要更有說服力的通膨加速跡象，才能讓委員會中較審慎的成員支持10月行動。

其他市場方面，美元指數上升0.34%至102.528，黃金期貨下跌1.15%至每盎司$4,129.10。WTI上漲0.93%至每桶$95.02，布蘭特原油上漲0.17%至$105.87。胡塞組織的新一波攻擊使沙烏地阿美總部受損，週三仍持續攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯各城市；沙國當局表示，總部無人傷亡。俄羅斯另稱，夜間攻擊了烏克蘭六座發電廠。9月物價數據顯示先前燃料衝擊的傳導範圍之際，新一輪攻擊又使能源實體供應安全承壓。紐約時間下午5時，API公布截至10月9日當週原油庫存減少1,110萬桶，前值減少209萬桶，市場原預期增加190萬桶。

## CoreWeave重挫，AI融資條件分化加深

CoreWeave最鮮明地反映了當日市場對融資的焦慮。2032年到期的無擔保債券跌破面額的78%，四個月前投資人仍以面額買進，如今殖利率超過15%；2031年與2032年到期的兩筆無擔保債均跌破面額的80%。5年期信用違約交換回到紀錄高點，Bloomberg週三報導所指的隱含五年違約機率超過50%。股價盤中最多下跌17%，收盤跌15%至$65.78。

同日刊出的訪談中，共同創辦人Brannin McBee卻提出截然不同的融資目標：CoreWeave繼3月首次讓以晶片擔保的債務取得投資等級評等後，希望持續取得這類評等，最終讓公司本身也取得投資等級，以接觸規模大得多的保險資金。這項目標與既有無擔保債券價格之間的落差，使高度依賴借款擴充容量的經營模式受到更嚴格檢視。

D.A. Davidson分析師Gil Luria認為，如果融資成本高於投資報酬，規模擴大反而可能讓經濟效益惡化。他以條件式比較說明：若以9%成本借款，最佳報酬卻只有5%，擴張會毀損價值，無法解決問題。他也認為，這次重新定價顯示公司可能連以9%借款都有困難。CoreWeave在7月的槓桿貸款融資，定價已高於原先希望的成本；依Bloomberg計算，這使每年利息支出增加約$3,000萬。

執行長Mike Intrator不認同市場評價。在經公司確認真實的內部備忘錄中，他表示未交付訂單金額足以支應債務義務，且綽綽有餘，並將部分賣壓歸因於競爭對手的融資及首次公開發行受挫。CoreWeave另以聲明表示，已簽約的未交付訂單足以完全支應有擔保債務及母公司無擔保債務的償還，不需客戶續約，也不需將擔保資產重新出租。Intrator計畫在下一次財報電話會議進一步回應市場反應。

疑慮也延伸至相關證券。一週內，至少七檔支應CoreWeave相關資料中心的債券下跌，包括Galaxy Digital與Core Scientific相關債務。標普7月對Galaxy債券的評估，曾指出一項具體期限錯配：CoreWeave與客戶的契約期限，比其對Galaxy承擔的租約期限短。標普警告，若AI需求不如預期且基礎設施供給過剩，租約履行可能更困難。這項契約風險與CoreWeave聲稱既有已簽約業務足以支應還款的立場並存。

股市加重了整個融資生態系的壓力。半導體指數週三下跌4.30%，連續六個交易日走低，累計市值蒸發約$1.6兆；逾半數成分股在這段期間跌幅至少10%。那斯達克100指數下跌2.02%，標普500下跌1.11%，VIX升至16.87。羅素2000下跌1.9%，進入3月以來首次技術性修正，下跌與上漲家數約為五比一，並較8月高點回落11%。利率上升不只壓抑估值昂貴的科技股，也對較小型借款人造成負擔。

實際營運需求仍有強勁跡象。ASML連續第三季調高全年銷售展望，並表示正尋求在未來兩年增加晶片製造設備產量的方法。瑞銀的Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi認為，科技股下跌是預期調整，而非AI投資基本面出現斷裂。Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou率領的摩根大通分析團隊則認為，市場支撐不如7月修正時有利，原因包括散戶逢低買進有限、庫藏股買盤轉弱、空頭部位不多，以及槓桿ETF資產規模更大。另一家受惠於資料中心建設的Caterpillar，股價較6月紀錄高點低約30%；Jefferies的Stephen Volkmann表示，機械需求雖強，但運費與原物料成本壓力使銷量對利潤率成長更加重要。

知情人士表示，Princeton Digital Group正洽談最高$12億的三年期聯貸，用於馬來西亞柔佛一座198.8百萬瓦園區，以及既有債務再融資。借款人將是旗下Labuan Alpha，安排行包括滙豐新加坡分行、Maybank Investment Bank、華僑銀行馬來西亞、渣打新加坡與大華銀行。這項申貸將具體專案納入區域借款計畫。

騰訊週二完成大額發債後，新披露的票息呈現另一種融資條件差異。10年期離岸人民幣債券票息為2.4%，比去年及6月發行的可比債券低10個基點；30年期票息為3%，相較之下，其美元債券殖利率超過6%。發行本身已為市場所知，新增的定價細節顯示，提高人民幣債務在融資中的占比有其成本優勢。CreditSights的Zerlina Zeng預期，資本支出增加、充裕的離岸人民幣流動性降低借款成本，將使中國科技業未來一年持續活躍發債。

不過，收盤時美國整體高收益債利差仍明顯擴大。HYG當日總報酬為負0.36%，投資等級債券基金LQD則上漲0.11%。美債反彈、風險較高的企業債下跌，顯示當日重點在於借款人的融資實力，而非所有債券朝同一方向變動。

## 遞延付息與再融資限制浮現

穆迪的統計顯示，私募信貸壓力不只反映在未按時付款。其評估的607家美國借款人，在截至6月的12個月內違約率為4%；若納入困境下的以債付息（PIK）條款修訂及展延到期日，則升至5.8%。穆迪將這類讓步列為困境債務交換，視同違約。

近期財務報表顯示，這些借款人有17%使用PIK付息。遞延現金支付可保留營運流動性，但利息加入本金後，債務會複利累積。穆迪發現，無論PIK在貸款成立時就已存在，或是後來加上，使用者普遍有流動性薄弱、自由現金流為負、槓桿偏高及利息保障能力接近損益兩平等問題。企業服務業借款人最集中出現流動性薄弱，軟體公司的整體信用指標則最弱。

即將到來的再融資負擔，也高度集中於較弱信用。2027年與2028年的到期債務，評等較低發行人均占逾半，使其更加依賴展延、進一步PIK修訂、昂貴的再融資或私募股權股東支持。不過，穆迪也指出，對資本結構中較優先順位的投資人而言仍有實質緩衝：借款人惡化尚未使中型企業貸款CLO顯著轉弱，投資組合管理、擔保品檢核及較強保護條款協助控制了損失。

澳洲私募信貸的壓力則來自放款機構本身的融資。知情人士表示，高盛與瑞銀對提供給基金管理機構的新融資愈來愈挑剔，偏好規模較大的一線業者，避開小型基金及高度曝險於困境房地產的機構，既有承諾大致仍予維持。近幾個月來，銀行已收緊條件，並在擁有核准權的情況下阻擋部分交易。

澳洲私募債務市場規模為A$2,000億，其中約一半與房地產有關，因此曝險不小。倉儲融資額度、以貸款組合擔保借款，以及銀行與基金分攤融資的架構，讓管理機構能投入更多資本；銀行通常持有優先債權，基金投資人先吸收損失。熟悉安排的人士表示，典型放款加碼利差約為現金利率之上350個基點，較廣泛的範圍為100至650個基點，這些加碼均另計於基準利息成本之上。

Zenith Investment Partners的Dugald Higgins警告，短期借款搭配長期私募投資，若投資人贖回增加，銀行融資縮減可能加重流動性壓力。Corval Avenue的Belinda Bible也表示，在投資人退縮之際，流動性減少可能帶來麻煩。浮動利率借款成本與住宅銷售轉弱，已使這些融資額度背後的房地產貸款承壓。銀行偏好優先順位曝險，說明了先前積極投入的部分原因，但借款基金仍須依賴再融資。

印度的情況則是擴張預測。Kotak Alternate的Srini Sriniwasan預期，全球與國內投資人未來兩年可向印度私募信貸投入最高$50億。他指出，銀行放款選擇性較高，債券市場又淺、集中於較高評等發行人，為另類資金留下成長空間。依EY資料，該市場2025年成長35%至$124億。Sriniwasan認為，印度央行採取匯率措施後，盧比波動減少可能吸引海外基金；Kotak另正為一檔國內房地產基金募集最高$3億，將以股權及債務投資辦公室、零售與其他領域。

退出條件也在改變私募股權基金的融資安排。新彙整數字顯示，今年私募股權基金出售資產給企業買家的交易約$4,500億，占全部退出交易90%；過去二十年間，這一比例僅另有三次達到。Galderma週三以$15億收購Blackstone支持的ZO Skin Health，也延續了這項趨勢。A&O Shearman的Neil Sinha表示，企業買家可憑立即實現的成本節省與較低的融資利差，合理支持較高出價；但槓桿收購利差收窄，也可能促成更多基金間轉售。Ropes & Gray的Aldo Piccarreta表示，大型私募股權基金正在思考：旗下公司規模已大，下一次退出時究竟誰有能力接手。

德國基礎設施業者Unsere Grüne Glasfaser（UGG）的債權人已聘請Lazard，就債務協商提供顧問服務。這家由Allianz Capital Partners與Telefónica支持的光纖業者，擁有€16.5億信用額度；原先尋求較單純的再融資，近期則在公司一方聘請Perella Weinberg。融資成本升高、寬頻採用速度較慢，正壓抑現金產生能力，網路建設卻仍需資金。雙方聘請顧問，意味討論已朝資產負債表調整移動，而不只是展延現有融資。

美國地方政府及相關機構借款人，也因殖利率升高，縮減已無法節省成本的交易。紐約大都會運輸署（MTA）將擬議再融資由$10.5億縮至$6.5億，最快可能10月19日發行。財務副主管Olga Chernat表示，不再符合節省目標的候選債券，將留待日後機會。本息支出約占其$228億營運預算14%，截至9月17日未償債務為$498億。新澤西運輸信託基金管理局也在本月稍早撤回$17億再融資，因為所需的節省效益已消失。

Nuveen最新第四季展望將此變化置於整體供給背景。8月符合再融資條件的債券，只有43%進行借新還舊，今年月均比例則為75%。截至第三季，借新還舊發行量年增20%，新資金發行僅增1%。Daniel Close與Margot Kleinman預期，部分發行人將等待更有利的利率，可能使供給低於其全年$6,000億估計；若需求回流，發行減少可協助市場穩定。

募集新資金的借款，仍有各自的信用重點。Hadran Academy計畫週四透過Build NYC Resource Corporation，發行約$5,600萬免稅收益債及$370萬應稅債務，用於布魯克林校區。標普給予BB評等，擔保包括總收入，主要是學費。約93%的學費由紐約市教育費用補助支應，至少75%的學生獲補助達學費80%或以上。擴建將使校區容量由目前144人增至250人。其還款基礎仰賴支撐收入的特殊教育補助安排，而非由市政府直接質押稅收。

## 各國央行對緊縮幅度看法分歧

曼谷會議期間，歐洲官員大致同意須警戒能源通膨，但對進一步緊縮應多快到來看法不同。歐洲央行總裁拉加德週三表示，尚未看到更廣泛經濟中的第二輪效應，正仔細檢視間接傳導；政策仍逐次會議決定，以中期2%通膨目標為重點。

比利時央行總裁Pierre Wunsch認為，可能還會再升息，但未選定10月或12月。他表示，通膨接近4%，使進一步行動成為合理的基本情境，然而能源與AI的不確定性，使時點難以確定。立陶宛央行的Gediminas Simkus另指出，9月通膨高於預期、能源成本超出估計，勞動市場仍強；12月將有更多資訊，但10月行動仍有可能。他同樣尚未看到明顯第二輪效應，不過能源昂貴維持愈久，向更廣泛領域傳導的機率愈高。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin強調，債券殖利率已帶來抑制效果。市場借款成本提高，可降低需求，容許較溫和的政策回應；家庭與企業的中期通膨預期仍穩定。Simkus也將主權債殖利率上升視為抵銷通膨的力量。兩人都將市場緊縮的效果納入政策利率決策考量。

這項區分也影響他們對法國的看法。Simkus認為，近期法國殖利率上升是在反映債務、政治及財政基本面，歐洲央行目前沒有介入角色。拉加德表示，首要解方在法國財政政策。Wunsch承認，傳導保護工具可用於不合理的市場變化，但不願推測是否動用。官員的判斷區分了合理的主權風險重新定價，以及可能需要購債介入的市場分裂。

英國央行首席經濟學家Huw Pill質疑的是市場預期緊縮的總幅度，而非最初方向。他自4月起一直支持立即升息，週三表示央行本應更早行動，但若要支持市場反映、截至明年夏季四次各25個基點、合計100個基點的升息，仍需更具體證據。未來六至九個月，薪資與物價是否持續傳遞衝擊，將是判斷核心。

總裁Andrew Bailey在週二晚間訪談中表示，能源衝擊持續愈久，愈難避免升息。他認為英國目前的第二輪效應較溫和，同時指出經濟活動增強。Bloomberg週三報導顯示，市場隱含的11月升息機率接近100%。

新加坡則實際暫停緊縮。新加坡金融管理局（MAS）在4月與7月收緊政策後，維持匯率政策區間的斜率、寬度與中心不變；受訪20位經濟學家中，只有三位預測此結果。MAS將今年核心通膨預測縮窄至1.5%至2%，先前上限為2.5%；預期2027年整體與核心通膨平均均為1.5%至2.5%。短期仍有輸入性壓力，但隨能源與食品供應干擾減退，2027年中起通膨放緩將更明顯。

第三季經濟成長初估由修正後的6.2%降至5.4%，為一年來最弱；製造業成長由12.9%降至7.5%。MAS仍認為，強勁AI訂單短期可支撐科技業活動，之後在2027年下半年轉緩。它指出，若市場大幅重估AI預期報酬，可能形成足以明顯削弱成長的金融衝擊，尤其當變現成果令人失望、使超大規模雲端業者縮減投資，並導致舉債支持的專案重新定價時。

泰國央行副總裁Piti Disyatat則界定了進一步寬鬆的條件。他表示，除非出現重大衝擊，目前1%的利率不太可能再降；正常利率約為1.5%至2%，回歸正常的速度將依經濟復甦、通膨及泰銖而定。他預期全年通膨約2%，低於先前2.8%的預測，成長則約為原估的2.3%，或略高。9月通膨雖升至2.82%，但成長低於潛力且家庭負債沉重，仍支持寬鬆立場。

波蘭決策官員Przemyslaw Litwiniuk也在匯率走弱之際，維持利率穩定的基本情境。他表示，茲羅提自5月底對歐元貶值3.1%後仍屬強勢，其對進口價格的影響並未主導政策討論。基準利率自3月以來維持3.75%。若11月預測顯示2027年下半年通膨超過3.5%，官員很可能考慮今年稍晚收緊政策。

## 主權融資選擇與亞洲債券需求分化

IMF週三的財政分析，為高殖利率與債務討論帶來最新估計。Era Dabla-Norris與Rodrigo Valdés警告，市場對財政風險愈來愈敏感，可能形成回饋循環：利息成本升高使債務負擔惡化，促使投資人要求更高殖利率。新預測顯示，全球有效平均利息成本將由2021年的2.3%升至2031年的3.7%；美國2031年利息支出將達GDP的5.7%，大致相當於預估的社會安全支出。若更多再融資集中於短天期，政策升息將更快傳入公共預算。

IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva另對美國財政部長Scott Bessent依靠成長改善債務動態的主張提出異議，認為成長無法夠快完成調整，還需要其他措施。Bessent主張，持續超過3%的成長有助降低債務占GDP比重。此時美國公共債務已逾$40兆、赤字接近$2兆；分歧在於調整速度與是否足夠，Bessent擬議的支出整頓方案細節仍待提出。

IMF另估計，英國若要在2030年前讓國防支出達GDP的3%，每年需另增£110億，融資計畫應在明年的支出檢討提出。Valdés認為，現有債務已高，不宜永久靠借款支應，稅負也已偏高，限制了增收選擇。Dabla-Norris表示，各部門支出的優先順序將面臨艱難取捨。

Legal & General披露其承擔主權風險方式的改變。這家管理£1.2兆資產機構的總體策略主管Chris Jeffery表示，公司在主要市場買進公債時，會搭配放空期貨避險，不再把每次殖利率急升都視為單純的買進機會。他提到AI借款、公共債務及可能升息，預期避險在可預見的未來將維持。若有證據顯示較高殖利率正使經濟放緩，或11月期中選舉後美國提出可信的財政計畫，可能改變他的判斷。這項部位安排反映他對債券愈來愈常與股票同跌的擔憂，儘管週三長天期美債反彈呈現了不同的單日結果。

阿根廷則為明確的融資缺口提出備案。經濟部長Luis Caputo週三表示，若無法透過受本國法律管轄的美元債券Bonares完成計畫中的再融資，政府可動用與中國的貨幣互換。其中$50億Bonar融資，是2027年$250億融資計畫的一部分。中國互換安排在8月續約五年，總額$190億，其中已啟用$50億。阿根廷主權風險由7月初410個基點升至約600個基點，Bonar發行也因美債殖利率偏高而於8月暫停。

Caputo將這個選項與另有的$200億美國互換安排區分；後者仍可用於平抑明年選舉前後的市場波動。他也告訴投資人，政府打算適時解決既有GDP認股權證的請求權問題。委內瑞拉經濟副總統Calixto Ortega則表示，債務永續性評估雖已接近完成，但地震干擾使公布延後。他承諾很快將有進一步重整措施，並重申反對全面美元化。民間估計債務約$1,700億，目前的新進展是政府對評估延誤的解釋，以及所表明的下一步。

烏干達在原定的緊急討論後實際升息。央行在連續八次會議未調整後，將基準利率由9.75%升至12%，為十五年來最大升幅。烏干達先令週三最多升值4%，達每美元3,984先令。總裁Michael Atingi-Ego指出能源通膨與貨幣貶值，預測未來12個月核心通膨為5.5%至6%、整體通膨為7%至7.5%，並表示匯率仍由市場決定。Alpha Capital的Stephen Kaboyo預期，本地債券報酬提高將吸引外匯資金流入；外匯存底有限，使利率政策成為主要回應手段。

中國最新貿易數字說明，國內刺激政策的討論仍不同於其他市場。9月出口年增36%，高於8月的25%；進口增加31%，當月順差接近$1,340億。高科技產品出口成長近64%，晶片及原物料價格上升也推高了名目貿易金額。美國銀行的Helen Qiao表示，強勁出口降低北京刺激內需的急迫性，但若成長弱到超出可容忍程度，可能促成另一輪支持方案。她支持降息、調降存款準備率並搭配財政措施，預期明年債券額度將與2026年相近。

外部回應則更趨限制。知情人士週三表示，德國希望歐盟將進口配額擴大至化學品、機械，可能還包括藥品，這是先前已宣布油電混合車安排之外的新推動。中國外銷蓬勃、內需疲弱，一方面給中國企業融資優勢，另一方面引來貿易夥伴更多抵制。

最新比較顯示，即使名目殖利率低，中國債券仍有國際報酬優勢。Bloomberg指數顯示，過去一年以美元計算的報酬接近10%，全球債券則虧損2.2%，美債虧損2.1%。該報導中，中國10年期殖利率為1.67%，較可比美債低352個基點，差距在本月稍早曾達紀錄高點362個基點。人民幣今年以來升值4.4%，是報酬的重要來源。不過，8月底外資持有額仍約人民幣2.03兆元，與去年底差異不大，強勁表現尚未帶來相應的海外持有量激增。

富達的Lei Zhu表示，已有投資人考慮由低配調回中性。宏利的Paula Chan預期，中國相對不受油價衝擊影響，加上國內高品質資產稀缺，將使殖利率維持穩定，並押注曲線趨平。Arkevium的Maxence Visseau認為，能否繼續勝出很大程度取決於人民幣；聯博的Eric Liu對主權債殖利率較不感興趣，認為離岸人民幣債券提供更好的溢酬。各方把報酬機會分別放在匯率、殖利率穩定及信用補償，而非一致預測主權債價格還會上漲。

日本債券估值也受到新的評估。摩根資產管理的Sylvia Sheng披露，已在9月買回平倉10年期日本公債空頭；三菱日聯的Kiyoshi Ishigane則在長期殖利率超過2.5%後，逐步減少低配。10年期殖利率接近3%，高於Topix的2.3%股息殖利率，差距為2005年有紀錄以來最大。本月日本公債期貨反彈，未平倉合約由9月的21.1萬口降至約18.6萬口。

政策解讀仍有分歧。Asset Management One的Yoshitaka Miura認為，美國對東京施壓，加上先前聯合匯率干預，使日本央行更快緊縮的可能性提高。Amundi的Claire Huang預期，更可信的通膨控制將使曲線趨平，短期利率上升，超長期殖利率則更穩定。Sheng仍維持日本股票超配，因全球風險而未直接買進日本公債；首相高市早苗支出計畫所需、尚未公布的發債規模，仍是其評估重點。這些披露的部位變動反映悲觀看法減輕，對財政及貨幣政策走向卻尚無共識。

## 後續市場焦點

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh將於紐約時間週四較晚時段在曼谷公開露面，是週六媒體靜默期開始前，下一次重要政策溝通。9月CPI使問題從官員先前釋出多少耐心，轉為更廣泛的基礎物價壓力是否改變10月27日至28日的決策。Goolsbee對需求的警告，以及褐皮書的供應鏈細節，使討論不再只圍繞汽油；房市疲弱與市場借款成本提高，仍是審慎行事的具體理由。

10月15日紐約時間上午8時30分，將公布9月生產者物價、零售銷售、每週失業救濟申請，以及兩項地區製造業調查。市場預期PPI月增0.5%，前值0.4%；核心PPI月增0.3%，前值0.2%。零售銷售成長預估由1.2%降至0.3%，初領失業救濟金人數預估20萬，前值19.7萬。紐約州製造業指數預估10.3，前值7.60；費城製造業指數預估28.4，前值37.8。這組數據將讓家庭支出、就業與生產，與物價壓力擴散的新證據一併接受檢視。

9月工業生產接著於10月16日公布，市場預期增加0.4%，前值持平。週五稍晚還有預算報告與8月TIC長期資金流，分別預估赤字$290億及淨流入$1,257億。中國週一公布的經濟活動數據，將檢驗Qiao附帶條件的刺激政策評估；經濟學家普遍預期第三季GDP年增4.5%。美國10月20日的房屋開工與初步建築許可，將在房貸申請之外，補充融資抑制效果的證據。

烏干達10月21日國庫券標售，是緊急升息後的下一項市場考驗；渣打的Samir Gadio關注殖利率需升高多少，才能穩定匯率。泰國10月28日利率決策將公布更新預測，為Piti所述利率下限提供背景。信用市場方面，CoreWeave已簽約的未交付訂單與租約義務、UGG債務協商，以及地方政府及相關機構發行人的再融資節省效益，仍分別決定能否取得融資。同時，沙烏地阿拉伯基礎設施與烏克蘭發電設施遭到新一波攻擊，使能源成本將持續多久仍不明朗，而各國央行正判斷還需要多大程度的緊縮。

9月核心CPI月增0.3%、年增2.6%，均高於預期。汽油帶動整體通膨加速，服務與科技產品價格又使壓力擴散。Goolsbee警告，AI投資可能使需求過熱；褐皮書則描述成本正沿供應鏈傳遞。期貨隱含的聯準會10月升息機率，盤中最高達55%，其後回到約40%。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Long-dated Treasuries recovered from an inflation-driven selloff on October 14 as a deepening retreat in technology shares brought buyers back to bonds, but the short end remained under pressure from renewed expectations of Federal Reserve tightening. The 10-year yield ended at 5.1854%, down 2.3 basis points, while the two-year edged up 0.85 basis point to 4.7975%. The curve flattened, and U.S. high-yield credit spreads widened noticeably.

September consumer prices supplied the day's decisive policy news. A gasoline-led acceleration was accompanied by stronger-than-expected underlying inflation, complicating the case for waiting until December to raise rates again. The Fed's regional business survey added evidence of costs spreading through supply chains, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned that AI investment might be overheating demand. Yet the session ended with falling long-term real yields rather than a sustained rise across the Treasury curve. CoreWeave's distressed bond prices and a sharp semiconductor selloff made the cost and durability of the AI buildout an immediate credit concern alongside the inflation shock.

## Inflation Broadens, but Long Treasuries Recover

The initial response to September CPI was forceful. Bloomberg's intraday account put the two-year yield as much as 16 basis points higher at 4.95%, while the five-year briefly exceeded 5.15%, a level last seen in 2007. Investors sharply increased their expectations for further tightening. Futures-implied odds of an October increase rose from around 20% before the release to as much as 55%, then settled near 40%. Two quarter-point increases were briefly fully priced by the end of January; later trading anticipated about 40 basis points by then.

The closing recovery was concentrated beyond the shortest maturities. Five-year yields fell 1.44 basis points to 4.9869%, and the 30-year declined 3.38 basis points to 5.5231%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 3.15 basis points to 38.79, while 2s30s contracted 4.23 to 72.56. As the equity selloff intensified, demand for bonds at elevated yields reversed most of the morning's losses. The final curve therefore combined a small increase in the policy-sensitive two-year yield with gains in intermediate and long debt.

The inflation-linked market preserved a less comfortable part of the CPI message. The 10-year real yield fell 3.67 basis points to 2.8248%, while 10-year breakeven inflation increased 1.37 basis points to 2.3606%. Lower real yields more than offset the increase in inflation compensation. Over the week, 10-year nominal yields were down 9.83 basis points and 30-year yields down 14.72; over the month, they remained higher by 21.74 and 16.91 basis points, respectively. The monthly increase at 10 years was still predominantly real: the inflation-adjusted yield was up 22.88 basis points, with breakevens 1.14 basis points lower.

Headline CPI increased 0.6% in September, up from 0.4% in August and matching the monthly consensus. Annual inflation nevertheless exceeded expectations, rising to 3.7% from 3.4%, against a 3.6% forecast. Excluding food and energy, prices increased 0.3%, unchanged from the previous month's pace but above the expected 0.2%. Annual core inflation reached 2.6%, compared with 2.4% previously and a 2.5% consensus. It was the second successive month of stronger-than-expected core inflation, and the last CPI release before the October 27-28 policy meeting.

Gasoline rose 9.1% month on month, but the detail extended beyond fuel. Medical-care services and owners' equivalent rent each increased 0.3%; used-car prices rose 0.7%, their largest monthly gain since October 2025. Airfares also increased, while grocery prices edged lower. Computer software and accessories were 28.4% more expensive than a year earlier, a record increase, and computers, peripherals and smart-home assistants rose a record 9.7%. Those technology categories put a measurable household-price dimension beside the enormous investment demand for computing capacity.

The distinction between an energy shock and more persistent inflation drew a new response from Goolsbee. Speaking Wednesday after the release, the Chicago Fed president called the figures discouraging and said services inflation showed that the pressure was not confined to categories affected by tariffs and the Iran war. He was more concerned that data-center construction and AI investment were overheating the economy, and said it was too early to know whether rates were high enough to restore inflation to 2%. His concern was demand-side persistence: once overheating builds, it becomes harder to remove.

The Beige Book, released Wednesday and based on information collected through October 5, gave that debate broader regional detail. Half of the Fed's 12 districts reported robust or intensifying price pressure. Businesses cited not only energy but other commodities, tariffs and insurance, with diesel surcharges carrying higher costs through supply chains. Most districts reported some economic growth, overall employment changed little or not at all, and eleven districts recorded at least some wage increases. Several reported inflation adding to pressure on pay.

The survey also showed why weak hiring did not necessarily mean weak production. More than two-thirds of surveyed Philadelphia manufacturers reported higher Q3 output, the largest share since Q2 2022, with growth extending beyond data centers, AI and defense. Dallas described stronger production and demand across durable and nondurable manufacturing, including oil-related spending and elevated refining and petrochemical activity. Kansas City manufacturers were increasing hours and overtime because workers were difficult to find or retain. In Cleveland, two banking contacts said AI and automation had reduced staffing needs by raising productivity.

Households and smaller businesses were absorbing a different side of those costs. New York contacts renewing health insurance described steep premium increases, higher deductibles and larger co-payments. St. Louis employers were transferring some insurance costs to workers, while some nonprofits reduced or eliminated employer-paid benefits. Atlanta reported stronger high-end retail alongside flat or declining demand at other price tiers; San Francisco contacts said financial pressure was spreading from lower-income into middle-income households. A separate Wednesday release showed inflation-adjusted hourly earnings falling year on year for a sixth consecutive month.

Housing supplied fresh evidence of monetary restraint. The MBA's 30-year mortgage rate rose 1 basis point to 7.50% in the week ended October 9, its highest since November 2023 and almost a percentage point above end-June. Purchase applications fell 4%, their sixth consecutive weekly decline and the longest losing stretch since July-August 2023. The purchase index dropped to 139.3 from 145.1. Refinancing fell for an eighth week, with its index at 513.5 versus 515.8; total applications declined 2.7%, following a 4.2% fall, and the overall index fell to 199.2 from 204.7. NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun expects higher rates to reduce Q4 closings, after earlier transactions had reflected contracts arranged before the latest financing squeeze.

Citi changed its policy forecast in response to the inflation breadth. Economists Veronica Clark and Andrew Hollenhorst now expect a quarter-point December increase, replacing their previous expectation of unchanged rates through Q1 2027, while still anticipating cuts afterward. PGIM's Robert Sockin said the release strengthened his existing forecast for an October hike. Principal Asset Management's Seema Shah and TD Securities' Oscar Munoz and Gennadiy Goldberg remained in the December camp, with TD arguing that higher market rates were already supplying some restraint. Janney's Guy LeBas thought a more convincing acceleration would be needed to bring cautious committee members behind an October move.

Across other markets, the Dollar Index rose 0.34% to 102.528, while gold futures fell 1.15% to $4,129.10 an ounce. WTI increased 0.93% to $95.02 a barrel and Brent rose 0.17% to $105.87. Fresh Houthi attacks damaged Saudi Aramco's headquarters and continued across Saudi cities Wednesday; Saudi authorities reported no casualties at the headquarters. Russia separately said it struck six Ukrainian electricity plants overnight. The renewed attacks kept physical energy security under pressure as the September price figures exposed the earlier fuel shock's reach. At 5 p.m. New York, API reported an 11.1 million-barrel crude-stock draw for the week of October 9, compared with a 2.09 million draw previously and expectations of a 1.9 million build.

## CoreWeave's Rout Sharpens the AI Financing Divide

CoreWeave became the clearest single-name expression of the day's financing anxiety. Its unsecured bonds due in 2032 traded below 78 cents on the dollar, although investors had bought them at par four months earlier, and yielded more than 15%. Both its 2031 and 2032 unsecured issues were below 80 cents. Five-year credit-default swaps returned to record levels and, in Bloomberg's Wednesday account, implied a default probability above 50% over that horizon. The shares ended down 15% at $65.78 after falling as much as 17% during the session.

The selling coincided with co-founder Brannin McBee's description of a very different financing ambition. In an interview published Wednesday, he said CoreWeave wanted to continue obtaining investment-grade ratings for chip-backed debt, as it first did in March, and eventually for the company itself. That would open a much larger pool of insurance capital. The gap between that goal and the price of existing unsecured debt heightened scrutiny of a business relying heavily on borrowing to fund its capacity expansion.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria argued that the economics could deteriorate with scale if funding costs exceeded investment returns. His comparison was conditional: borrowing at 9% to earn a best return of 5% would destroy value rather than cure the problem through expansion. He also said the repricing suggested difficulty borrowing even at 9%. CoreWeave's July leveraged-loan financing had already priced above its intended cost, adding roughly $30 million in annual interest expense, according to Bloomberg's calculation.

Chief executive Mike Intrator disputed the market's assessment. In an internal memo authenticated by the company, he said its backlog more than supported its debt obligations and attributed some of the selling to financing and IPO setbacks at competitors. In a separate statement, CoreWeave said contracted backlog fully supported repayment of secured debt and unsecured parent obligations without customer renewals or re-leasing collateral. Intrator plans to address the reaction further at the next earnings call.

The concern was spreading into related securities. At least seven bonds backing data centers tied to CoreWeave traded lower during the week, including debt associated with Galaxy Digital and Core Scientific. A July S&P assessment of Galaxy's bonds had identified a specific maturity mismatch: CoreWeave's customer contracts were shorter than its lease commitments to Galaxy. S&P warned that weaker-than-expected AI demand and excess infrastructure supply could make those leases harder to honor. That contractual exposure sits alongside CoreWeave's assertion that its existing contracted business supports repayment.

Equities magnified the pressure on the financing ecosystem. The semiconductor index fell 4.30% Wednesday, extending a six-session slide that erased about $1.6 trillion of market value. More than half its constituents had lost at least 10% over that run. The Nasdaq 100 declined 2.02%, the S&P 500 lost 1.11%, and the VIX rose to 16.87. The Russell 2000 fell 1.9%, entering its first technical correction since March, with about five declining stocks for every advancing one and an 11% retreat from its August high. Higher rates were weighing on smaller borrowers as well as expensive technology shares.

Strong operating demand was still visible. ASML raised its annual sales outlook for a third successive quarter and said it was looking for ways to produce more chip-making equipment over the next two years. UBS's Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi regarded the technology decline as an expectations adjustment rather than a fundamental break in AI investment. JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou saw less favorable market support than during July's correction, citing limited retail dip-buying, weaker buyback flows, a small short base and larger leveraged-ETF assets. Caterpillar, another beneficiary of data-center construction, traded about 30% below its June record; Jefferies' Stephen Volkmann said robust machinery demand was meeting freight and raw-material pressure that made sales volumes more important to margin growth.

Funding continued for other Asian operators. Princeton Digital Group is seeking a three-year syndicated loan of up to $1.2 billion for a 198.8-megawatt campus in Johor, Malaysia, and existing-debt refinancing, according to a person familiar with the proposal. Its Labuan Alpha subsidiary would borrow the proceeds, with HSBC's Singapore branch, Maybank Investment Bank, OCBC Malaysia, Standard Chartered Singapore and UOB arranging the facility. The request adds a defined project to a regional borrowing plan rather than a completed loan.

Tencent's newly reported coupons illustrated another source of differentiation after its large sale Tuesday. The 10-year offshore yuan tranche carried 2.4%, 10 basis points below comparable notes sold last year and in June, and the 30-year carried 3%, against yields above 6% on its dollar notes. The offering's execution was already known; the new pricing detail showed the advantage of directing more of the financing into yuan debt. CreditSights' Zerlina Zeng expects Chinese technology issuance to stay strong over the next year as capital spending rises and abundant offshore yuan liquidity lowers borrowing costs.

Broader U.S. high-yield spreads nevertheless widened noticeably at the close. HYG's daily total return was negative 0.36%, while investment-grade fund LQD gained 0.11%. The Treasury recovery and losses in riskier corporate debt left borrowers' financing strength, rather than a uniform bond-market direction, central to the session.

## Deferred Interest and Refinancing Limits Come Into Focus

Moody's supplied a new measure of private-credit stress that was not captured by missed payments alone. Among 607 U.S. borrowers it assessed, the default rate was 4% in the 12 months through June. Including distressed payment-in-kind amendments and maturity extensions raised it to 5.8%. Moody's classifies those concessions as distressed exchanges equivalent to default. The comparison concerns that historical sample and period, rather than a new daily default count.

Recent statements showed 17% of those borrowers using PIK interest. Deferring cash payments can preserve operating liquidity, but adding interest to principal compounds debt. Moody's found weak liquidity, negative free cash flow, high leverage and interest coverage near break-even among PIK users, whether the feature existed at origination or was added later. Business-services borrowers had the greatest concentration of weak liquidity; software companies had the weakest overall credit metrics.

The approaching refinancing burden was heavily concentrated in weaker credits. Lower-rated issuers accounted for more than half of maturities in both 2027 and 2028, increasing dependence on extensions, further PIK amendments, expensive refinancing or sponsor support. Moody's also reported a substantive buffer for investors further up the structure: borrower deterioration had not yet produced significant weakness in middle-market CLOs, where portfolio management, collateral tests and stronger protections had helped contain losses.

Australian private credit faced pressure through the funding of the lenders themselves. Goldman Sachs and UBS are becoming more selective about new financing to managers, favoring larger, top-tier firms and avoiding smaller funds or heavy exposure to troubled real estate, people familiar with the business said. Existing commitments are largely being maintained. The shift has developed over recent months and includes tighter terms and, where banks have approval rights, blocked transactions.

The exposure is substantial because roughly half of Australia's A$200 billion private-debt market is linked to property. Warehouse facilities, borrowing against loan portfolios and split bank-and-fund structures have allowed managers to deploy more capital, while banks generally hold senior claims and fund investors absorb losses first. People familiar with the arrangements put a typical lending margin near 350 basis points above the cash rate, within a broader range of 100-650 basis points. Those margins are additional to the benchmark interest cost.

Zenith Investment Partners' Dugald Higgins warned that reduced bank funding could add liquidity stress if investor redemptions increased, given the combination of short borrowing and long private investments. Corval Avenue's Belinda Bible likewise said shrinking liquidity could be troublesome while investors were pulling back. Floating-rate borrower costs and weaker home sales were already straining the property loans beneath those facilities. The banks' preference for senior exposure helps explain their earlier appetite without removing the refinancing dependence of the funds borrowing from them.

India presented a contrasting expansion forecast. Kotak Alternate's Srini Sriniwasan expects global and domestic investors to commit as much as $5 billion to Indian private credit over the next two years. He cited selective bank lending and a shallow bond market concentrated in higher-rated issuers as reasons for alternative capital to grow. The market expanded 35% to $12.4 billion in 2025, according to EY. Sriniwasan argued that reduced rupee volatility after the RBI's currency measures could attract overseas funds; Kotak is separately raising up to $300 million for a domestic real-estate fund investing in both equity and debt across offices, retail and other segments.

Exit conditions were also reshaping sponsor financing. Newly compiled figures showed roughly $450 billion of private-equity sales to corporate buyers this year, or 90% of total PE disposals, a proportion reached only three other times in two decades. Galderma's Wednesday purchase of Blackstone-backed ZO Skin Health for $1.5 billion added to that pattern. A&O Shearman's Neil Sinha said corporate buyers can justify higher prices through immediate cost savings and tighter financing margins, while noting that narrower LBO spreads could support more sponsor-to-sponsor deals. Ropes & Gray's Aldo Piccarreta said large sponsors were asking who could buy an already-large portfolio company at their next exit.

In German infrastructure, Unsere Grüne Glasfaser's creditors appointed Lazard to advise on debt talks. The Allianz Capital Partners- and Telefónica-backed fiber operator has a €1.65 billion credit line and recently brought in Perella Weinberg on its own side, after previously seeking a more straightforward refinancing. Higher financing costs and slower broadband take-up are pressuring cash generation while network construction still requires funding. The advisers' appointments move the discussion toward the balance sheet rather than merely extending the existing financing.

Municipal borrowers were responding to higher yields by reducing transactions that no longer delivered savings. New York's MTA cut its planned refinancing to $650 million from $1.05 billion, with a sale possible as early as October 19. Deputy finance official Olga Chernat said candidates that no longer met savings targets would be held for later opportunities. Principal and interest payments account for about 14% of its $22.8 billion operating budget, and the agency had $49.8 billion of outstanding debt as of September 17. New Jersey's Transportation Trust Fund Authority separately pulled a $1.7 billion refinancing earlier this month because the necessary savings had disappeared.

Nuveen's new Q4 outlook put the change in a broader supply context. Only 43% of bonds eligible for refinancing in August were refunded, compared with a monthly average of 75% this year. Refunding supply through Q3 was up 20% from a year earlier, while new-money issuance increased only 1%. Daniel Close and Margot Kleinman expect some issuers to wait for better rates, potentially reducing supply below their $600 billion full-year estimate. They argued that lower issuance could help the market stabilize if demand returned.

New-money borrowing still had distinct credit considerations. Hadran Academy plans about $56 million of tax-exempt revenue bonds and $3.7 million of taxable debt Thursday through Build NYC Resource Corporation for a Brooklyn campus. S&P assigned a BB rating; security includes gross revenues, chiefly tuition. Approximately 93% of school fees are covered by New York City education reimbursements, with at least 75% of pupils receiving reimbursement of 80% or more of tuition. The expansion would lift campus capacity to 250 students from 144 currently. Its repayment base depends on the special-education reimbursement arrangements supporting that revenue, rather than tax receipts pledged directly by the city.

## Central Banks Disagree on How Far Tightening Must Go

At the Bangkok meetings, European officials largely agreed that energy inflation required vigilance but differed over how rapidly further restraint should arrive. ECB President Christine Lagarde said Wednesday that officials were not yet seeing second-round effects in the broader economy and were examining indirect transmission carefully. She kept policy guidance meeting-by-meeting and focused on the 2% medium-term objective.

Belgian central-bank governor Pierre Wunsch said another increase was likely, without choosing October or December. Inflation approaching 4% made further action a reasonable base case, but energy and AI uncertainty prevented a firm timing judgment. Lithuania's Gediminas Simkus separately pointed to above-expected September inflation, higher-than-anticipated energy costs and a still-strong labor market. December would offer more information, he said, while October action remained possible. He also saw no evident second-round effects yet, but warned that longer-lasting expensive energy increased the chance of broader transmission.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin emphasized the restraint already coming from bond yields. Higher market borrowing costs could reduce demand and allow a more moderate policy response, he said, while medium-term household and corporate inflation expectations remained anchored. Simkus similarly identified rising sovereign yields as a counterforce to inflation. Their comments placed market tightening beside policy-rate decisions, rather than assuming each rise in government yields required an equal increase in central-bank rates.

The distinction also shaped their response to France. Simkus regarded recent French yield increases as pricing debt, politics and fiscal fundamentals, and saw no current role for ECB intervention. Lagarde said the first solution lay in French fiscal policy. Wunsch acknowledged the availability of the Transmission Protection Instrument for unwarranted developments, but declined to speculate on its use. The officials' assessments leave an important difference between legitimate sovereign-risk repricing and fragmentation that might justify purchases.

In Britain, Chief Economist Huw Pill challenged the scale rather than the initial direction of market tightening expectations. A persistent supporter of an immediate increase since April, he said Wednesday that the BOE should have acted sooner but would need more concrete evidence to justify the 100 basis points implied by four quarter-point increases by next summer. Evidence over the next six to nine months of wages and prices propagating the shock would be central to that judgment.

Governor Andrew Bailey, in a late-Tuesday interview, said a longer energy shock made avoiding an increase harder. He described second-round effects as more subdued in Britain so far, while noting stronger activity. Bloomberg's Wednesday account put market-implied odds of a November increase near 100%. Pill's skepticism about the full sequence therefore came from an official who had already favored the first step, giving it a different meaning from opposition to tightening altogether.

Singapore delivered an actual pause. MAS left the slope, width and center of its exchange-rate policy band unchanged after April and July tightening, a decision predicted by only three of 20 surveyed economists. It narrowed this year's core-inflation forecast to 1.5%-2%, from an earlier upper bound of 2.5%, and expects both headline and core inflation to average 1.5%-2.5% in 2027. It anticipates near-term imported pressure but more discernible easing from mid-2027 as energy and food disruptions abate.

Advance Q3 growth slowed to 5.4% from a revised 6.2%, the weakest pace in a year, while manufacturing growth eased to 7.5% from 12.9%. MAS still sees strong AI orders supporting technology activity in the near term, before moderation in the latter half of 2027. It described a sharp reassessment of expected AI returns as the kind of financial shock that could materially weaken growth, especially if disappointing monetization led hyperscalers to curtail investment and debt-funded projects were repriced. That conditional forecast accompanied the hold; it was not an assessment that such a contraction had already occurred.

Thailand's Deputy Governor Piti Disyatat supplied a separate boundary for easing. He said the current 1% rate was unlikely to fall further without a major shock, and put a normal rate around 1.5%-2%, with normalization paced by recovery, inflation and the baht. He expects full-year inflation near 2%, below the previous 2.8% forecast, and growth around the earlier 2.3% estimate or slightly higher. September inflation had risen to 2.82%, but below-potential growth and heavy household debt still justified an accommodative stance.

Polish policymaker Przemyslaw Litwiniuk likewise retained a stable-rate base case despite currency weakness. He said the zloty remained strong after losing 3.1% against the euro since end-May, and that its import-price effect had not dominated policy discussions. The benchmark has been 3.75% since March. If November projections show inflation above 3.5% in H2 2027, he said, officials would probably consider tightening later this year. That forecast threshold, rather than the exchange-rate decline alone, defines his stated condition for a change.

## Sovereign Funding Choices and Asian Bond Demand Diverge

The IMF's Wednesday fiscal analysis added fresh estimates to the debate over high yields and debt. Era Dabla-Norris and Rodrigo Valdés warned that growing sensitivity to fiscal risk could create a feedback loop: higher interest costs worsen debt burdens, encouraging investors to demand still higher yields. Their new projections put the global effective average interest cost at 3.7% by 2031, up from 2.3% in 2021, and U.S. interest payments at 5.7% of GDP in 2031, roughly matching projected Social Security spending. More refinancing at short maturities would transmit policy increases into public budgets faster.

Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva separately challenged Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's reliance on growth to improve U.S. debt dynamics, saying growth would not deliver the adjustment quickly enough and other measures were necessary. Bessent has argued that sustained growth above 3% would help lower debt relative to GDP. The disagreement comes with public debt above $40 trillion and a deficit near $2 trillion. It concerns the speed and sufficiency of adjustment, with details of Bessent's proposed spending-consolidation package still pending.

Britain received a specific spending warning. The IMF said an additional annual £11 billion would be needed to reach defense spending of 3% of GDP by 2030, with financing plans due at next year's spending review. Valdés argued that high existing debt made borrowing unsuitable as a permanent answer and that already-high tax burdens limited revenue options. Dabla-Norris said departmental priorities would involve difficult tradeoffs. The fresh defense-cost assessment adds a concrete demand on the budget rather than another general call for consolidation.

Legal & General disclosed a change in how it was absorbing sovereign risk. Chris Jeffery, macro-strategy head at the £1.2 trillion manager, said the firm was hedging government-bond purchases through short futures across major markets instead of treating every yield spike as an unqualified buying opportunity. He cited AI borrowing, public debt and potential rate increases, and expects the hedges to remain for the foreseeable future. Evidence that higher yields were slowing the economy, or a credible U.S. fiscal plan after the November midterms, could change his assessment. The positioning reflects his concern that bonds have increasingly fallen alongside equities, even though Wednesday's long-Treasury recovery provided a different daily outcome.

Argentina identified a contingency for a defined financing gap. Economy Minister Luis Caputo said Wednesday that the government could use its China currency swap if planned refinancing through local-law dollar bonds, known as Bonares, proved impossible. A $5 billion Bonar component belongs to the $25 billion 2027 financing program. The Chinese swap, renewed in August for five years, totals $19 billion and includes an activated $5 billion portion. Sovereign risk had risen to about 600 basis points from 410 in early July, and Bonar issuance was paused in August amid high Treasury yields.

Caputo distinguished that option from Argentina's separate $20 billion U.S. swap, which remains available to calm market volatility around next year's election. He also told investors the government intended to resolve legacy GDP-warrant claims in due course. In Venezuela, Economy Vice President Calixto Ortega said earthquake disruption had delayed publication of the debt-sustainability assessment, despite work having been nearly ready. He promised further restructuring steps soon and reiterated opposition to full dollarization. Private estimates put debt near $170 billion; the immediate development is the government's explanation for the assessment delay and stated next step.

Uganda moved from a scheduled emergency discussion to a realized rate increase. The central bank raised its benchmark to 12% from 9.75%, its largest increase in 15 years, after eight meetings without a change. The shilling gained as much as 4% to 3,984 per dollar Wednesday. Governor Michael Atingi-Ego cited energy inflation and depreciation, projecting core inflation of 5.5%-6% and headline inflation of 7%-7.5% over the next 12 months. He said the exchange rate remained market-determined. Alpha Capital's Stephen Kaboyo expects higher local-bond returns to attract currency flows, with reserve limitations making rate policy the principal response.

China's new trade figures showed why its domestic stimulus debate remained different. September exports rose 36% year on year after 25% in August, imports increased 31%, and the monthly surplus approached $134 billion. High-tech shipments rose almost 64%, while higher chip and commodity prices also inflated nominal trade values. Bank of America's Helen Qiao said strong exports had reduced Beijing's urgency to stimulate domestic demand, but weaker-than-tolerable growth could prompt another support package. She favors rate and reserve-requirement cuts alongside fiscal measures and expects next year's bond quota to be similar to 2026's.

The external response was becoming more restrictive. Germany wants EU import quotas extended to chemicals, machinery and potentially pharmaceuticals, people familiar with the plans said Wednesday. That is a new push beyond the previously announced hybrid-car arrangement. Beijing's booming external sales and weak domestic demand were producing both a financing advantage for Chinese firms and more resistance from their trading partners.

New comparisons showed Chinese bonds' international return advantage despite low nominal yields. Bloomberg indexes put their dollar-based return near 10% over the past year, against a 2.2% loss for global debt and a 2.1% Treasury loss. China's 10-year yield was 1.67%, with a 352-basis-point discount to comparable Treasuries in that account; the gap had reached a record 362 basis points earlier in the month. The yuan's 4.4% year-to-date rise was an important contributor. Foreign holdings were still about 2.03 trillion yuan at end-August, little changed from year-end, so strong performance had not yet brought a comparable surge in overseas ownership.

Fidelity's Lei Zhu reported interest from investors considering moving from underweight toward neutral. Manulife's Paula Chan expects yields to remain anchored by relative insulation from the oil shock and scarcity of high-quality domestic assets, and is betting on curve flattening. Arkevium's Maxence Visseau sees further outperformance depending importantly on the yuan. AllianceBernstein's Eric Liu was less attracted to sovereign yields and saw better premiums in offshore yuan bonds. Their differing assessments locate the return opportunity in currency, yield stability and credit compensation rather than in a single forecast of further sovereign price gains.

Japan also drew a fresh reassessment of bond valuations. JPMorgan Asset Management's Sylvia Sheng disclosed that she closed 10-year JGB shorts in September, while Mitsubishi UFJ's Kiyoshi Ishigane has been reducing his underweight as long yields moved above 2.5%. With the 10-year near 3%, its yield exceeded the Topix's 2.3% dividend yield by the widest margin since records began in 2005. JGB futures open interest had fallen to about 186,000 contracts from 211,000 in September as futures recovered this month.

The policy interpretation remained contested. Asset Management One's Yoshitaka Miura thought Washington's pressure on Tokyo and the earlier joint currency intervention made a faster BOJ tightening cycle more likely. Amundi's Claire Huang expects stronger inflation-control credibility to flatten the curve, with short rates rising and ultra-long yields better anchored. Sheng has stayed overweight Japanese equities and is not buying JGBs outright amid global risks; the still-unannounced issuance needed for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's spending plans remains important to her assessment. The disclosed positioning change marks reduced bearishness, not agreement on a completed fiscal or monetary shift.

## Forward Market Significance

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's late-Thursday New York appearance in Bangkok is the next major policy communication before the media blackout begins Saturday. September CPI has changed the question from how much patience officials have signaled to whether broader underlying pressure alters the October 27-28 decision. Goolsbee's demand warning and the Beige Book's supply-chain detail give that discussion a wider basis than gasoline alone, while housing weakness and higher market borrowing costs remain concrete reasons for caution.

October 15 brings September producer prices, retail sales, weekly claims and the two regional manufacturing surveys at 8:30 a.m. New York. Consensus expects PPI to rise 0.5% after 0.4%, and core PPI 0.3% after 0.2%. Retail-sales growth is expected to slow to 0.3% from 1.2%; claims are expected at 200,000 against 197,000. The Empire State index is forecast at 10.3 after 7.60, and Philadelphia's at 28.4 after 37.8. The combination will put household spending, employment and production beside the new evidence of broadening prices.

September industrial production follows October 16, with a 0.4% consensus after no change. The budget statement and August long-term TIC flows arrive later Friday, with expectations of a $29 billion deficit and $125.7 billion net inflows, respectively. China's Monday activity releases will test Qiao's conditional stimulus assessment; economists broadly expect Q3 GDP growth of 4.5% year on year. U.S. housing starts and preliminary permits on October 20 will add to the mortgage-application evidence of financing restraint.

Uganda's October 21 bill auction is the next market test of its emergency increase, with Standard Chartered's Samir Gadio focusing on how far yields rise to stabilize the currency. Thailand's October 28 decision will bring updated forecasts behind Piti's rate-floor guidance. For credit, CoreWeave's contracted backlog and lease obligations, UGG's debt negotiations and municipal issuers' refinancing savings remain separate determinants of funding access. Meanwhile, the fresh attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Ukrainian power facilities leave the persistence of energy costs unresolved at the point when central banks are deciding how much further restraint is needed.

overall_summary.headline: Technology selling revives long Treasuries despite broader inflation and renewed Fed tightening expectations
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Long Treasuries reversed an inflation-driven selloff as technology shares retreated on October 14. The 10-year yield fell 2.3 basis points to 5.1854%, while the 2-year rose 0.85 basis point to 4.7975%, narrowing the 2s10s spread by 3.15 basis points to 38.79. The recovery came through real yields: the 10-year real yield fell 3.67 basis points to 2.8248%, more than offsetting a 1.37-basis-point rise in breakeven inflation to 2.3606%.

September core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% on the year, both above expectations. Gasoline led the headline acceleration, but services and technology prices broadened the pressure. Goolsbee warned that AI investment could be overheating demand, and the Beige Book described costs spreading through supply chains. Futures-implied odds of an October Fed increase settled near 40% after reaching 55% intraday.

The semiconductor index fell 4.30%, extending a six-session decline, while CoreWeave shares lost 15%. Its unsecured bonds due in 2032 traded below 78 cents on the dollar and yielded more than 15%, despite management's assertion that contracted backlog fully supports debt repayment. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably even as long Treasuries recovered. Strong AI operating demand remained visible at ASML, leaving the cost and durability of debt-funded expansion, rather than a uniform collapse in demand, central to the credit concern. Warsh's next appearance and the October 15 data will test how broader inflation changes the October policy decision.
